Further plots: Tucker factors, cause shares and backtest scores

Source: R/plot.R
mt_plot_more.Rd

  • mt_plot_tucker(): the factor matrices of a tucker3() fit (age, period and stratum modes), one panel per mode and one line per factor; signs are arbitrary.

  • mt_plot_shares(): shares of each cause in the deaths over the selected ages, observed and forecast (median and 95% interval), from a forecast with a cause variable among the strata (for example from cause_shares()).

  • mt_plot_scores(): mean score of each model by horizon or age from a backtest, or one bar per model (by = "model"); target selects rates or a derived quantity scored by the backtest.

Usage

mt_plot_tucker(fit)

mt_plot_shares(
  draws,
  var = NULL,
  total_level = NULL,
  ages = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  causes = NULL
)

mt_plot_scores(
  backtest,
  metric = "crps",
  by = c("horizon", "age", "model"),
  target = c("rate", "life_expectancy", "asr", "life_expectancy_gap", "asr_gap")
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted tucker3() model.

draws

An mt_draws object whose strata include var.

var

Stratum variable with the causes (default: the variable with shared exposures in the hierarchy of a reconciled forecast).

total_level

Level of var for all causes (left out of the shares; default: its total in the hierarchy).

ages

Age labels summed over (default all).

groups

Panels to show: combinations of the other stratum variables joined by "." (for example "female.Q1"; default all).

causes

Levels of var to show (default all; shares are always computed among all levels).

backtest

An mt_backtest() result.

metric

Score column, for example "crps", "wis" or "ae".

by

"horizon", "age" or "model".

target

"rate", "life_expectancy" or "asr" (see mt_backtest()).

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 2000:2019)
  mt_plot_tucker(mt_fit(tucker3(), x))
  bt <- rbind(mt_backtest(rwd(), x, origins = c(2012, 2014), h = 4, n_draws = 50),
              mt_backtest(lee_carter(), x, origins = c(2012, 2014), h = 4, n_draws = 50))
  mt_plot_scores(bt)
}
